subcategory: education regulation — private schools, homeschooling, online learning
name: British Columbia — independent schools, online learning and homeschooling
description: B.C. regulates non-public schools under the Independent School Act. Schools are classified Group 1–4; Groups 1 and 2 receive operating grants of 50% and 35% of the local district per-student amount and must use B.C.-certified teachers and meet ministry program requirements; Group 3 is unfunded with a lighter regime; Group 4 serves mainly international students. Families may homeschool (register by 30 September, no supervision, no Dogwood) or enrol in a funded online learning school (teacher-supervised, Dogwood possible).

attributes.legal_term: Independent school (Independent School Act, RSBC 1996 c.216)

classification.group_1: Non-profit authority; B.C.-certified teachers and principal; ministry instructional-time and program requirements; Grades 10–12 meet graduation requirements; provincial assessments; per-student operating cost not above local district grant; external evaluation at least every 6 years and inspection at least every 2 years; grant = 50% of local district per-student amount.
classification.group_2: As Group 1 except per-student operating cost exceeds the local district grant; grant = 35%.
classification.group_3: At least 50% eligible (resident) students; evaluation at least every 2 years; no grant; teacher-certification and curriculum rules not stated on the classification page.
classification.group_4: Mostly international students; certified teachers required to offer the certified graduation program; bond required; external evaluation every 2 years; no grant.

attributes.diploma: B.C. Certificate of Graduation (Dogwood) available through Group 1, 2 and 4 schools with certified graduation programs and through online learning schools; homeschoolers are not eligible.
attributes.online_learning: Since 2023 'distributed learning' is called online learning (Bill 8, 2020). Independent online learning schools are Group 1 schools with a ministry agreement; the ministry lists 15 (updated 2025-09-10), funded at 50% (Group 1) of the public online-learning FTE rate (35% for Group 2). Learning is supervised by a B.C. teacher.
attributes.homeschooling: Register each child with a public or a willing independent school by 30 September; parents direct the whole program; not supervised, inspected or required to meet provincial standards; registering school receives $250 (public) or $175 (Group 1/2) per child — nothing to parents; no Dogwood; Grades 10–12 may combine homeschool registration with online courses; immunisation reminders at ages 4–6, 11, 14.
attributes.funding_to_families: None directly. Tuition at Group 1/2 schools is reduced by the operating grant.
attributes.parent_obligations: Compulsory schooling is satisfied by enrolment in a public or independent school, an online learning school, or registered homeschooling.
attributes.newcomer_note: Funding and online-learning eligibility depend on the student being an 'eligible' (B.C.-resident) student; enrolment forms ask for citizenship/permanent-resident or permit documents.

sources.title: Bill 8 – 2020 (Education Statutes Amendment Act) — online learning terminology

limitations: Group 3 teacher/curriculum obligations not stated on the page read. Date the 'online learning' terminology took effect (1 July 2023) rests on a school-district page.
